title: Before mandatory APP reimbursement, reported loss reimbursement varied sharply across UK banking groups
source_unit: Payment Systems Regulator 2024 APP scam performance report for transactions before the mandatory reimbursement requirement
geography: United Kingdom; customers of the 14 largest banking groups using Faster Payments

observations.period: Transactions before 7 October 2024; cases closed in 2024

denominator.unit: UK banking groups in the PSR reported provider comparison

reported_loss_reimbursement_by_value.value: Nationwide 85%; TSB 80%; Barclays 77%; NatWest/RBS/Ulster 75%; Santander 73%; Metro Bank 70%; HSBC/First Direct 68%; Clydesdale/Virgin Money 67%; Co-operative Bank 62%; Starling 55%; Lloyds/Bank of Scotland/Halifax 49%; AIB 31%; Monzo 25%; Danske Bank 24%
reported_loss_reimbursement_by_value.unit: percent of reported APP scam losses refunded by value, provider-group comparison

overall_reimbursement.unit: percent of reported APP scam loss value reimbursed across the comparison

provider_spread.unit: percentage-point gap between the highest and lowest reported provider rates

mandatory_rule_status.value: The comparison predates the mandatory APP reimbursement requirement that began on 7 October 2024

individual_receipt_and_adequacy.unit: missing unique victims, individual payment amounts, residual loss, claim effort, household consequence, trust, switching, and later recovery

observations.method: Transcription of the PSR provider-comparison chart for transactions before 7 October 2024 and cases closed in 2024; provider groups are retained as reported and are not treated as causal firm effects.
observations.uncertainty: The source is a provider-level administrative comparison, not a randomized design or person-level panel. Firm mixes, scam types, reporting, claim eligibility, case composition, and reimbursement definitions may differ; the pre-policy rates cannot be mechanically compared with the later dashboard's post-policy denominator.
observations.subgroup: Customers reporting APP scam losses to the 14 largest banking groups; the comparison does not represent all UK payment firms or all scam victims.
observations.counterinterpretation: Provider variation may reflect customer mix, scam composition, investigation practice, policy interpretation, or receiving-firm dynamics rather than a simple difference in fairness or willingness to reimburse.

boundary: This record adds a provider-level pre-policy baseline for reported APP-scam loss reimbursement. It does not estimate causal bank effects, individual adequacy, household recovery, or a before/after policy effect; it must be kept separate from the post-October-2024 PSR reimbursement dashboard.

related_sources.claim: The PSR publishes the provider-comparison data and identifies the 7 October 2024 mandatory reimbursement start as the policy boundary.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official PSR PDF downloaded and hashed on 2026-10-20; provider percentages and the aggregate comparison are transcribed from the report's accessible chart text.
